entries.overview: CPython is the reference Python implementation and source tree, not a third-party Python learning package. The checked main README labels itself Python 3.16 alpha development; that is not a stable-release recommendation.
entries.requirements: To build on Unix-like systems, consult the official Developer Guide for platform-specific dependencies, a C toolchain and optional libraries. On Windows use PCbuild instructions. End users normally install official stable binaries rather than compiling main.
entries.quickStart: For source exploration read README.rst and Developer Guide, clone a tagged stable release only if a local build is required, then follow platform build instructions and test. No commands executed.
entries.costAndDeployment: Source available without licensing fee. Builds run locally; compute and maintenance cost depend on platform. No hosted API is required to read or compile the source.
alternatives: PyPy for a different Python implementation
Official prebuilt CPython releases for users who do not need source builds
entries.limitations: Main development README may change daily. GitHub license API NOASSERTION does not mean absence of license. Activity and stars are a timestamped API snapshot, not a popularity trend.
researchIdeas: Map how parser/compiler/runtime stages connect with evidence from official source files.
Build a compatibility matrix of language changes against stable Python releases.

entries.overview: Godot is an open-source 2D/3D game engine with an editor and export options for desktop, mobile and web. Console distribution has additional platform requirements and should not be assumed to be a one-click public export.
entries.requirements: For ordinary use download the official editor and suitable export templates. Building the engine from source requires platform-specific dependencies documented by the Godot maintainers.
entries.quickStart: Download the editor from the official site, read the beginner documentation and open an official demo project. For engine development follow the compilation guide. No commands executed.
entries.costAndDeployment: MIT-licensed engine with no engine royalties. Platform distribution, hardware, asset licensing, and console access can still have separate costs and conditions. Can run locally without a hosted AI service.
alternatives: Unreal Engine for another 3D engine workflow
entries.limitations: Stars and last push are metadata snapshots only. The core engine MIT license does not automatically license all third-party assets, demos or platform SDKs.
researchIdeas: Compare Godot 3D scene performance on a fixed public demo across supported renderers.
Create a verified 3D car interaction tutorial using licensed reference images and tested controls.
